chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever pleases a ruler by incurring the anger of Allah, has exited from the religion of Islam.'

key_terms.بِسَخَطِ اللَّهِ: By incurring the anger of God

ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of pleasing a ruler by angering God according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shia political theology, this hadith establishes the principle of 'exit from Islam' (kharaj min al-Islam) not merely as a legal status but as a spiritual rupture caused by compromising divine truth for temporal power. It underscores the critical distinction between the 'Sultan' (ruler) and the 'Creator', warning that subjugating one's conscience to political expediency while violating God's command constitutes a fundamental breach of faith. This concept is central to the Shia understanding of justice (Adl) and the independence of religious authority from political coercion.
